items.stem:
The mean mass of the 12 boys in a class is 48.5 kg.
The mean mass of the 8 girls in the same class is 44 kg.

parts.t: Calculate the total mass of the 12 boys.
Calculate the mean mass of all 20 students in the class.

sols: Total mass of the boys = 48.5 × 12 = 582 kg
Total mass of the girls = 44 × 8 = 352 kg
Total mass of the class = 582 + 352 = 934 kg
The answer lies between 44 and 48.5 and is closer to 48.5, because there are more boys than girls ✓

The lower quartile is the 20th value.
Reading across from 20 and down to the time axis gives 20.
The upper quartile is the 60th value: reading across from 60 gives 40 minutes.
Interquartile range = upper quartile − lower quartile
Read up from 45 minutes to the curve: the cumulative frequency is 65.

items.stem:
120 students took an examination marked out of 100.
The cumulative frequency diagram shows their marks.

parts.t: Find the median mark.

The students with the highest 25% of marks are awarded a distinction.
Find the lowest mark that is awarded a distinction.

The pass mark is 45.
Find the number of students who fail the examination.

sols: Read across from 60 on the cumulative frequency axis to the curve, then down.
25% of 120 = 30 students get a distinction, so 120 − 30 = 90 do not.
The lowest distinction mark is the mark at cumulative frequency 90 (the upper quartile).
Reading across from 90 and down gives 67
Read up from a mark of 45 to the curve and across: the cumulative frequency is 34.
34 students scored less than 45 and fail.
ms:
M1 for 90 seen or a line drawn from cf = 90
A1 accept 66 to 68

The histogram shows the ages, a years, of the people at a concert.
The frequency density axis has no scale.
There were 30 people aged 10 < a ≤ 15.

parts.t: Work out the total number of people at the concert.
Estimate the number of people aged between 35 and 45.

sols: In a histogram, frequency is proportional to the area of the bar.
Count the large grid squares: the bar for 10 < a ≤ 15 is 1 large square wide (5 years) and 6 large squares tall, so its area is 6 large squares.
one large square = 5 years by 1 unit of height
6 large squares represent 30 people, so 1 large square represents 5 people.
Bar 0–10: 2 × 2 = 4 squares = 20 people; bar 15–25: 2 × 4.5 = 9 squares = 45 people; bar 25–45: 4 × 1.5 = 6 squares = 30 people
width × height in large squares, then × 5
Ages 35 to 45 make up 10 of the 20 years in the class 25 < a ≤ 45, and the histogram assumes ages are spread evenly within a class.
ms:
M1 for 30 ÷ (area of the 10–15 bar) oe to find what one square represents
M1 for at least two other frequencies correct (20, 45, 30)
A1 cao

B1
FT half of their frequency for 25 < a ≤ 45

The weekly wages, in dollars, of the 8 people who work in a small shop are

320    340    340    360    380    400    420    1600

parts.t: Calculate the mean wage.
Find the median wage.

The shop advertises for a new worker using the average wage.
Which average, the mean or the median, better represents a typical wage? Give a reason for your answer.

sols: The wages are already in order. There are 8 values, so the median is halfway between the 4th and 5th.
Seven of the eight workers earn less than the mean of 520; the mean is pulled up by the single very large wage of 1600.
an extreme value (outlier) affects the mean but not the median
The median, because it is not affected by the one very high wage of 1600.
ms: Median, not affected by the extreme value 1600

B1
must choose the median and refer to the 1600 or to an extreme/outlier value

The mean mark of 25 students in a test is 62.
The teacher then finds that one mark was recorded as 45 when it should have been 54.

parts.t: Calculate the correct mean mark of the 25 students.

A 26th student then takes the test and scores 88.
Calculate the mean mark of all 26 students.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: The correction adds 54 − 45 = 9 to the total: 1550 + 9 = 1559
